questions.scenario: A property-management company extracts 14 fields from 25,000 lease applications per month with Claude, using a tool with a JSON schema. Quality control is a random 5% sample sent to two reviewers. Monthly audits keep finding the same pattern: 80% of the errors come from handwritten or photographed applications, which are 12% of volume, and they cluster in `monthly_income` and `employer_name`. The random sample rarely includes enough of those documents for reviewers to catch them, and reviewer capacity cannot grow. The model already outputs a confidence value per field, calibrated last month against a labeled set. What is the most effective change to the review process?
options: Double the random sample to 10% and split it evenly between the two reviewers, so that more of the handwritten applications end up in the review queue
Add an instruction to the extraction prompt asking the model to be especially careful with handwritten and photographed documents before filling the fields
Send every handwritten or photographed application to review and auto-approve all digital ones, so reviewers focus only on the 12% that cause errors
Route to review the fields whose calibrated confidence is low, plus documents with risky characteristics such as handwriting, instead of a random sample
questions.why_correct: El objetivo pide rutear por confianza, características del documento y ambigüedad por campo, no por muestreo aleatorio. La guía: rutear extracciones con baja confianza o documentos ambiguos a revisión humana, priorizando la capacidad limitada. Ya tienen confianza calibrada por campo: úsenla, sumada a la señal "manuscrito".

why_wrong.0: Duplicar el muestreo aleatorio no cabe en la capacidad fija, y sigue mandando sobre todo documentos digitales que casi nunca fallan.
why_wrong.1: Pedir cuidado en el prompt es guidance; no cambia qué ve el revisor. Puede mejorar algo, pero no es un diseño de ruteo.
why_wrong.2: Casi correcta, pero gruesa: manda los 14 campos de todos los manuscritos (3.000 docs) aunque la mayoría de campos estén bien, y auto-aprueba digitales sin mirar su confianza. Ignora la señal por campo que ya tienen.

questions.rule: Revisión humana: ruteá por confianza calibrada por campo + características del documento, no al azar.
questions.source_quote: Routing extractions with low model confidence or ambiguous/contradictory source documents to human review, prioritizing limited reviewer capacity

questions.scenario: An expense-management startup extracts merchant, date, total and tax from receipts using Claude. On a labeled set of 6,000 receipts, overall field accuracy is 97%. The CFO wants to turn off human review entirely next month to cut costs. A data analyst notes that the labeled set mixes printed PDF receipts (70%), thermal paper photos (20%) and foreign-currency receipts (10%), and that nobody has broken the accuracy down. The extraction prompt and schema are stable and the team has two weeks before the decision. What should the team do first?
options: Measure accuracy by document type and by field on the labeled set, and only reduce review for segments that perform consistently well
Turn off review for receipts where the model's self-reported confidence is above 90%, since the overall accuracy already exceeds the target
Keep a 5% random sample under human review after turning it off for everything else, so any drop in overall accuracy gets detected early
Add 2,000 more labeled receipts to the evaluation set to make the 97% figure statistically stronger before presenting it to the CFO
questions.why_correct: Un 97% agregado puede esconder un desempeño malo en un tipo de documento o un campo puntual (por ejemplo `tax` en tickets térmicos). La guía pide validar la precisión por tipo de documento y por campo ANTES de automatizar, y reducir la revisión solo donde el desempeño es consistente.

why_wrong.1: La confianza autorreportada sin calibrar no es un criterio confiable, y "el 97% ya supera el target" es justo el número agregado que puede mentir.
why_wrong.2: Un muestreo aleatorio del total detecta caídas en el promedio, pero no te dice si un segmento chico ya está mal desde el día uno.
why_wrong.3: Más datos hacen más preciso el MISMO número agregado; el problema es que no está desglosado, no que tenga poca muestra.

questions.rule: Antes de apagar revisión: precisión por tipo de documento y por campo, no el promedio global.
questions.source_quote: The risk that aggregate accuracy metrics (e.g., 97% overall) may mask poor performance on specific document types or fields

questions.scenario: A customs broker extracts 22 fields from commercial invoices. For each field, the extraction tool returns a `confidence` between 0 and 1 produced by the model. The team routes any field below 0.80 to review because "0.80 sounds reasonable". After a month, auditors find that fields scored between 0.85 and 0.95 have a 14% error rate on `hs_code`, while `invoice_date` fields scored 0.60 are almost always correct. Reviewers are overloaded with dates and miss the HS codes. The team has 1,500 invoices already labeled by senior brokers. What is the most effective fix?
options: Add few-shot examples to the prompt showing the model when to report lower confidence for HS codes, so its scores become more conservative on that field
Lower the global threshold to 0.70 so that fewer date fields reach the queue, freeing reviewer time that can then be spent on the HS code errors
Calibrate per-field thresholds against the 1,500 labeled invoices, measuring the real error rate at each confidence level for each field
Replace the numeric score with a categorical `high`/`medium`/`low` field, which is easier for the model to report consistently across fields
questions.why_correct: El puntaje crudo no está calibrado: 0.90 en `hs_code` no significa lo mismo que 0.60 en `invoice_date`. La guía dice: que el modelo dé confianza por campo y después calibrar los umbrales con un set de validación etiquetado. Tienen 1.500 facturas etiquetadas: midan error real por nivel y por campo.

why_wrong.0: Few-shot para "bajar la confianza" es casi tentadora, pero sigue confiando en el número que el modelo se pone a sí mismo, sin medir contra la verdad. Puede mover los puntajes sin hacerlos calibrados.
why_wrong.1: Un umbral global más bajo saca fechas pero también saca HS codes; el problema es que un mismo umbral no sirve para todos los campos.
why_wrong.3: Cambiar a categorías cambia el formato, no la calibración: "high" seguiría sin significar una tasa de error medida.

questions.rule: Umbral de confianza elegido "a ojo" → calibralo por campo contra un set etiquetado.
questions.source_quote: Having models output field-level confidence scores, then calibrating review thresholds using labeled validation sets

questions.scenario: A utility company automated high-confidence extractions from meter-reading forms after validating each form type and field: anything above the calibrated threshold goes straight into billing with no human review. Five months later, a regional contractor starts submitting a new form layout where the meter ID and account number columns are swapped. The model extracts both with high confidence, so none of these forms reach a reviewer, and the problem is discovered only when 3,400 customers receive wrong bills. The labeled validation set has not changed since launch. What should have been in place to catch this earlier?
options: A monthly re-run of the original labeled validation set to confirm that accuracy on each form type stays above the threshold used at launch
Ongoing stratified random sampling of auto-approved high-confidence extractions, to measure error rates and detect new error patterns
A rule that sends every form to human review whenever the model's confidence on any field falls below the calibrated threshold for that field
A stricter JSON schema for the meter ID and account number, with `strict: true` so that values that do not follow the expected format are rejected
questions.why_correct: Lo de alta confianza no lo mira nadie, y un patrón de error nuevo puede aparecer justo ahí. La guía pide muestreo aleatorio estratificado de las extracciones de alta confianza para medir la tasa de error en curso y detectar patrones nuevos. Un revisor habría visto columnas cruzadas en las primeras semanas.

why_wrong.0: Casi correcta, pero el set etiquetado es de la época del lanzamiento: no tiene el layout nuevo, así que seguiría dando bien mientras producción falla.
why_wrong.2: Eso ya existe (es el ruteo por umbral) y por definición no atrapa errores con confianza ALTA, que es lo que pasó.
why_wrong.3: Si los dos IDs tienen formato parecido, el schema valida forma, no que el valor esté en el campo correcto: se cumplía igual con las columnas cruzadas.

questions.rule: Automatizaste lo de alta confianza → igual muestreá (estratificado) esa porción para detectar errores nuevos.
questions.source_quote: Implementing stratified random sampling of high-confidence extractions for ongoing error rate measurement and novel pattern detection

questions.scenario: A commercial real-estate firm extracts `payment_term_days` and `renewal_notice_days` from lease contracts. In about 4% of leases, the main body and an annex disagree, for example clause 4 says 30 days and Annex B says 45. The model picks one value and reports high confidence, so these leases are auto-approved; finance discovered the conflicts only after late-payment disputes. The schema currently has `payment_term_days: integer` and a per-field `confidence` number. Reviewer capacity is limited, so the team does not want to send all leases with annexes to review. Which change addresses the root cause?
options: Add a per-field status enum (`found`, `not_found`, `conflicting`) with the competing values, and route `conflicting` fields to review regardless of confidence
Instruct the model to always prefer the value in the main body of the contract, since annexes are usually older, and to lower its confidence when an annex exists
Make `payment_term_days` nullable so the model can return null when it is unsure, and route every lease with a null in that field to human review
Send every lease that contains an annex to human review, since annexes are the source of the conflicting values that the model resolves incorrectly
questions.why_correct: Los documentos contradictorios tienen que ir a revisión humana aunque el modelo esté "seguro" (la guía nombra explícitamente las fuentes ambiguas o contradictorias). Para eso el schema tiene que poder EXPRESAR el conflicto: un enum con `conflicting` y los valores en pugna. Así se rutea solo el 4% que lo necesita.

why_wrong.1: Inventar una regla de precedencia es decidir una cuestión legal en el prompt; la cláusula del anexo puede ser la vigente. Y "bajar la confianza" sigue dependiendo del autorreporte.
why_wrong.2: Es casi correcta: nullable ayuda contra inventar datos. Pero acá el dato SÍ existe dos veces; null mezcla "no está" con "hay dos valores" y pierde los valores en pugna que el revisor necesita.
why_wrong.3: Mandar todos los contratos con anexo desborda la capacidad: la mayoría de los anexos no contradicen nada.

questions.rule: Fuentes contradictorias → el schema tiene que poder decir `conflicting`, y eso va a revisión sin importar la confianza.
questions.source_quote: Routing extractions with low model confidence or ambiguous/contradictory source documents to human review, prioritizing limited reviewer capacity

questions.scenario: A B2B payments company extracts supplier invoices with Claude via the Message Batches API overnight. Each morning, about 1,800 invoices are flagged for human review because at least one field fell below its calibrated threshold, but the four reviewers can only clear 300 per day. The queue is processed first-in, first-out, so a €480,000 invoice with an uncertain IBAN waited six days while reviewers checked low-value invoices with an uncertain `po_number`. Late payments on large invoices triggered penalties last quarter. Reviewer headcount is fixed. What is the most effective improvement?
options: Move extraction from the Message Batches API to the synchronous Messages API so invoices are flagged as they arrive and the queue builds up more evenly
Raise every field's confidence threshold so fewer invoices are flagged each night and the four reviewers can clear the whole queue within a single day
Define risk tiers combining which field is uncertain (IBAN, amount) with the invoice value, and have reviewers work from the highest tier down
Ask the model to add a `priority` field to each extraction stating how urgent it believes a review is, and sort the review queue by that field
questions.why_correct: La capacidad es fija; lo que falta es priorizar. La guía pide rutear priorizando la capacidad limitada de revisores, y la guía de moderación muestra el patrón: varios niveles de riesgo para ajustar cuán agresivo es el tratamiento de cada uno. Un IBAN dudoso en una factura enorme vale más revisión que un `po_number` en una chica.

why_wrong.0: Pasar a sincrónico cambia cuándo llegan, no cuántas hay ni cuáles importan más. Y pierde el descuento de Batches sin resolver nada.
why_wrong.1: Subir umbrales para que entre en la cola es esconder incertidumbre: las facturas grandes dudosas pasarían a pago automático.
why_wrong.3: La prioridad autorreportada por el modelo no está calibrada ni conoce el costo de negocio de cada error; no es una base confiable para ordenar.

questions.rule: Más casos dudosos que revisores → niveles de riesgo (qué campo + cuánto vale) y revisar de mayor a menor.
questions.source_quote: Creating multiple risk levels allows you to adjust the aggressiveness of your moderation. For example, you might want to automatically block user queries that are deemed high risk, whereas users with many medium risk queries are flagged for human review.

questions.scenario: A bank extracts 30 fields from scanned account-opening forms. Each field gets a calibrated confidence, but routing is decided per document: if any field is below its threshold, the whole form goes to a reviewer, who re-checks all 30 fields against the scan. Logs show that 62% of forms are flagged, almost always because of one or two fields (usually `occupation` or a second phone number), and reviewers spend about 9 minutes per form. Compliance requires a human to confirm every low-confidence value. The team wants to cut review time without lowering accuracy. What is the most effective change?
options: Lower the thresholds for `occupation` and secondary phone numbers so those fields stop triggering a review of the whole form so frequently
Route at field level: show reviewers only the fields below threshold, with their scan region, and auto-accept fields above their thresholds
Add more few-shot examples for `occupation` and phone numbers to the prompt so the model reports higher confidence on those two fields
Split the 30 fields across three extraction calls of 10 fields each, so a low-confidence field only flags one third of the form for review
questions.why_correct: La confianza ya es por campo; el ruteo no. La guía habla de confianza a nivel de campo para dirigir la ATENCIÓN de revisión. Mostrar solo los campos dudosos cumple compliance (un humano confirma cada valor de baja confianza) y elimina la re-revisión de 28 campos que ya estaban bien.

why_wrong.0: Bajar umbrales para que dejen de saltar viola compliance: valores que hoy son de baja confianza pasarían sin humano.
why_wrong.2: Subir la confianza que REPORTA el modelo no lo hace más preciso; sin recalibrar, solo esconde la duda.
why_wrong.3: Partir las llamadas reduce la revisión a un tercio del formulario, pero sigue revisando campos que no lo necesitan, y triplica las llamadas. Es un parche del ruteo por bloque.

questions.rule: Confianza por campo → ruteo y revisión por campo, no por documento entero.
questions.source_quote: Field-level confidence scores calibrated using labeled validation sets for routing review attention

questions.scenario: An insurer extracts claim data from a standard claim form with Claude. Thresholds were calibrated in March on 2,000 labeled forms, and stratified sampling of auto-approved extractions has run weekly since then. In September the insurer released version 4 of the form, which moved the incident date into a table. This week's sample shows the error rate on `incident_date` for v4 forms at 19%, versus under 1% for v3 forms; other fields and versions look normal. About 30% of incoming forms are now v4. Claims must be paid within 10 days. What should the team do first?
options: Double the stratified sampling rate across all form versions for the next month to confirm whether the 19% error rate is real before taking any action
Lower the confidence threshold for `incident_date` across every form version, so many more of those fields go to human review starting this week
Update the extraction prompt with an example of the v4 table layout and redeploy it immediately, since the new layout is clearly the cause of the errors
Route `incident_date` on v4 forms to human review now, and recalibrate that threshold on newly labeled v4 forms before automating it again
questions.why_correct: El muestreo hizo su trabajo: detectó un patrón nuevo en un segmento (v4, un campo). La guía pide validar por tipo de documento y por segmento de campo antes de automatizar lo de alta confianza. Primero frenás el daño en ese segmento (revisión humana) y después recalibrás con datos etiquetados de v4.

why_wrong.0: Duplicar el muestreo de todo retrasa la acción mientras el 19% de error sigue pagando reclamos; además ya está claro en qué segmento está el problema.
why_wrong.1: Un umbral más bajo para todas las versiones inunda la cola con fechas de v3 que funcionan bien, y no está claro que atrape los errores de v4 (que pueden tener confianza alta).
why_wrong.2: Mejorar el prompt puede ser parte de la solución, pero redesplegar sin validar contra datos etiquetados de v4 es automatizar a ciegas otra vez.

questions.rule: El muestreo encuentra un segmento roto → revisión humana para ESE segmento y recalibrar con datos etiquetados antes de reautomatizar.
questions.source_quote: The importance of validating accuracy by document type and field segment before automating high-confidence extractions

questions.scenario: A healthcare billing firm asks Claude to return, for each of 18 fields extracted from insurance claims, a `confidence` from 1 to 10. Routing sends anything below 7 to coders. Three months of data show that 93% of field scores are 9 or 10, and errors are spread almost evenly across scores 8, 9 and 10; the score barely separates good extractions from bad ones. The team has 900 claims double-coded by senior staff. An engineer proposes changing the scale to 0-100 for more granularity. What is the most effective response?
options: Treat the raw score as uncalibrated: measure real error rates per field and score level on the 900 labeled claims, and set thresholds from that
Adopt the 0-100 scale as proposed, because the wider range lets the model express smaller differences in certainty between similar extractions
Add an instruction that the model must not give a score of 10 unless the value appears verbatim in the claim, to spread the scores more evenly
Drop confidence scores and route a fixed random 20% of claims to the coders, since the scores have been shown to be unreliable for routing
questions.why_correct: Un número que el modelo se pone a sí mismo no es confianza calibrada; la guía advierte que la confianza autorreportada es un proxy poco confiable, y propone calibrar los umbrales con un set de validación etiquetado. Con 900 claims doble-codificados pueden medir qué tasa de error real hay en cada nivel y campo.

why_wrong.1: Más granularidad sobre una escala sin calibrar da números más finos igual de poco informativos.
why_wrong.2: Puede abrir un poco la distribución, pero sigue siendo autorreporte sin medir contra la verdad; es casi correcta pero no resuelve la calibración.
why_wrong.3: Volver al muestreo aleatorio tira la posibilidad de rutear por señal; el objetivo es justamente rutear por confianza calibrada, no al azar.

questions.rule: Confianza autorreportada que no separa aciertos de errores → calibrala contra datos etiquetados; no cambies la escala.
questions.source_quote: Field-level confidence scores calibrated using labeled validation sets for routing review attention

questions.scenario: A legal-tech company extracts 12 clauses from commercial leases using Claude with the Citations feature enabled on the PDF documents. The response is parsed line by line into `field: value` pairs, and each line's citations are attached. Fields with a value are auto-approved. An audit found that about 3% of auto-approved values, mostly `break_clause_date` and `rent_review_basis`, have no citation at all, and several of them do not appear anywhere in the lease. Reviewer capacity is limited and the team does not want to review every field. What change should they make to the routing logic?
options: Turn on structured outputs with a strict schema for the 12 fields, since a schema-compliant response guarantees that every field is supported by the document
Ask the model in the prompt to only state values that it can cite, and keep auto-approving every field that comes back with a non-empty value
Check that each field has a value and at least one citation, and route fields without a supporting citation to human review instead of approving them
Send every lease that contains a `break_clause_date` or `rent_review_basis` to human review, since those two fields concentrate the uncited values
questions.why_correct: La doc de Citations es explícita: chequeá que cada campo tenga un valor y al menos una cita, porque la API no garantiza ninguna de las dos cosas. Un campo sin cita es una señal barata y por campo de que el valor puede no estar en el documento: va a revisión, el resto sigue automático.

why_wrong.0: Structured outputs garantiza que la respuesta cumpla el schema, no que el valor esté respaldado por el documento. Un valor inventado puede ser perfectamente schema-compliant.
why_wrong.1: Pedirlo en el prompt es guidance; la doc dice que la API no garantiza ni el valor ni la cita, así que hay que chequearlo en código.
why_wrong.3: Rutea por nombre de campo, no por la señal real: manda a revisión los 97% de esos campos que sí tienen cita y desperdicia capacidad.

questions.rule: Extracción con Citations: campo sin cita → revisión humana. La API no garantiza ni valor ni cita.
questions.source_quote: Check that each field has a value and at least one citation. The API doesn’t guarantee either.

questions.scenario: A retailer's customer-support resolution agent issues refunds based on data extracted from customer-uploaded receipts (merchant, date, total). The extraction step reports 96% overall accuracy, and today every receipt is auto-approved. A segment analysis on 3,000 labeled receipts shows: printed receipts 99% on `total`, e-mail screenshots 98%, but faded thermal-paper photos only 71% on `total`, while `merchant` and `date` stay above 97% on all types. Thermal photos are 15% of volume. Two support specialists are available to review, and refund fraud is a growing concern. Which routing design best uses this analysis?
options: Route every thermal-paper receipt to the two specialists for a full review of all fields, and auto-approve the printed receipts and the e-mail screenshots
Route the `total` of thermal-paper photos to the specialists, auto-approve the other segments and fields, and keep sampling auto-approved receipts
Keep auto-approving everything, but add an instruction telling the agent to ask the customer to confirm the total when the photo looks faded or blurry
Lower the global confidence threshold for `total` across all receipt types so that more of the uncertain totals reach the two specialists for review
questions.why_correct: El análisis por segmento dice exactamente dónde está el problema: el campo `total` en fotos térmicas. Rutear por característica del documento Y por campo usa la capacidad chica en lo que importa, y el muestreo de lo auto-aprobado vigila que no aparezcan errores nuevos.

why_wrong.0: Casi correcta, pero revisa también `merchant` y `date` de esas fotos, que están arriba del 97%: gasta capacidad de dos personas donde no hace falta y no deja vigilancia sobre lo auto-aprobado.
why_wrong.2: Delegar en que el agente "note" que la foto está borrosa es guidance sin respaldo de datos; el análisis ya identificó el segmento, no hace falta adivinar.
why_wrong.3: Un umbral global para `total` manda también totales de recibos impresos (99% de precisión) y no apunta al segmento que falla.

questions.rule: El análisis por segmento te dice QUÉ campo de QUÉ tipo de documento revisar: ruteá eso, no documentos enteros ni todo.
questions.source_quote: Analyzing accuracy by document type and field to verify consistent performance across all segments before reducing human review
